correctness.rationale: The key nonstandard bounds are proved: a nonaffine 8-set has at most 2 antiperiods, hence at least 13 distinct nonzero differences, while its balanced sign has at least four nonzero Walsh coefficients, hence at most 11 Fourier zeros. The contradiction forces every spectrum to be an affine hyperplane. Fourier inversion equates orthogonality on a hyperplane with complementation by its annihilator. Hyperplane support transversals give 256 spectra. One- and two-antiperiod double counting gives 10080, 1920, 840, 30 exactly; all quantifiers and counting conventions are explicit. Standalone integer enumeration exhaustively verifies all 12870 supports.

originality.rationale: The novel object is the full partner multiplicity distribution and exact ordered incidence count for all eight-point subsets of the Walsh group F_2^4. The finite-group weak-tiling result gives existence implications, not these quantities; cyclic primitive-set theorems are on a different character group. A specialized eigenvalue paper remains an explicitly recorded unresolved bibliographic risk, but the accessible scientific evidence provides no dominating incidence classification.

value.rationale: All 8-point supports in the 16-point Boolean character group are a natural complete classification domain. The theorem gives a structural antiperiod criterion, identifies every spectrum, explains a large gap between the nonaffine bound of 4 and the affine count of 256, and yields the exact 14880 incidence count for Sylvester-Walsh Hadamard 8×8 minors. This is information not implied by mere spectrality or tile-existence and has reusable Fourier-sparsity/translation structure. Its finite scope is explicit.
